data.name: Bapon
data.gender_notes: Bapon is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bhag-Pat', meaning 'Lord of Wealth' or 'Lord of Fortune'. In Hindu mythology, Bapon is an alternate name for Lord Vishnu, who is the preserver of the universe and the god of wealth. The name Bapon carries the meaning “Lord of Wealth” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bapon usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bapon belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Wealth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bapon total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Bapon' holds significant cultural importance in Bengali Hindu tradition. In various rituals and ceremonies, Bapon is considered an auspicious name and the deity Bapon is worshiped to seek blessings for wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. It is believed that invoking the name Bapon can bring abundance and success in business and financial endeavors.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Bapon' signifies the devotion and faith in the divine power of Lord Vishnu as the protector and provider. By seeking the blessings of Bapon, one expresses their trust and reliance on the divine power to provide for their needs and aspirations, and to protect them from any misfortune or hardship. It also encourages the practice of self-discipline and virtuous living, as the blessing of wealth and prosperity is seen as a reward for good deeds and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bapon is a title of reverence in Hinduism, often used to address spiritual teachers or enlightened beings. It symbolizes deep respect, devotion, and a seeking of wisdom and guidance from the guru. The syllables "ba" and "pon" in Bapon represent the aspirant's humility and yearning for the teacher's blessings, signifying the guru-disciple relationship based on mutual respect and trust.

historical_references.reference: Bapon was a famous Bengali poet and philosopher during the medieval period. He was a contemporary of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and is believed to have influenced his thought.

Bapon is also known as Srinath Chakraborty Thakur. He wrote in the Bengali language and is best known for his works 'Bhagavad-vijay' and 'Bhagavat-khanda'. These texts are significant in the development of Bengali devotional literature.
